findings.text: the landed change supersedes this assertion (`assert "working" in rendered`) and leaves it failing: logs/sibling_base.log is 13 passed / EXIT=0 at 6c9489c95 and logs/sibling_head.log is 12 passed 1 failed / EXIT=1 at 09089a1e9 on tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py::test_a_pane_following_both_projects_draws_the_reset_once, so promoting this node alone turns the suite red; the worker was fenced out of the file and declared it under outside_scope with the one-line repair, and the repair must land with this node.

RESET_INSTRUCTION is appended to every limit-reset row whatever its group, so a reset recorded under a worker budget group prints `orchestrator sessions may continue` — measured in logs/sibling_head.log, whose claude-sub/seven_day row renders `limit reset · claude-sub · seven_day · orchestrator sessions may continue`; that record establishes nothing about orchestrator sessions, and this is the group whose 2026-10-22 reset had to be clarified to thirteen sessions as not applying across lanes.

RESET_CLOCK_CLAUSE and RESET_REASON_CLAUSE re-parse the prose composed by lift_watch._reset_detail (reckon/crew/lift_watch.py:382-385), so that sentence's punctuation and wording become a second hardcoded contract; a reworded sentence silently drops the clock and the reason from every pane row with no failure anywhere, which is the fallback the docstring describes but no test exercises.

`assert GROUP in rendered` and `assert CLOCK in rendered` at :120-121 assert values the fixture itself passed through _announce into mark_used, and both already appear in the base revision's render (`limit claude-orchestrators new → working` in logs/base.log), so neither can fail on the regression the change guards; the guard rests on :119 and :122-123, which do redden.

the landing record says the renderer returns to `ticker.Painter.render`, but reckon/crew/ticker.py:2598 defines the class as `Ticker` and no `Painter` exists in the package, so a reader following the record's own pointer finds nothing.
